reasoning: Both attempts provide a shared module of live screen facts, a single-UIScale ScreenGui wrapper, a touch layout chosen from PreferredInput or screen size, and a top-anchored layout clear of the touch controls. B wins on the deciding criteria. It replaces the title's UITextSizeConstraint cap with a fixed TextSize so the title grows on 4K, where A leaves the 24 px cap unscaled. B also clamps the scale to at least 1, while A's pointer path shrinks to 0.8. B's const and string-require churn is a style and runtime risk but passes every check.

criteria.note: UI/Responsive.luau exposes viewportSize, inputKind, scale, canvasSize and sizeClass as Vide sources. They update on ViewportSize, CurrentCamera and PreferredInput changes.

criteria.criterion: 2. Large screens grow via one UIScale
criteria.note: Screen.luau binds a single UIScale to Responsive.scale (short side / 1080 on pointer devices). The touch path caps the scale at 1.6, and the pointer path can go down to 0.8.

criteria.criterion: 3. Small screens change layout, not shrink
criteria.note: Touch or Compact screens switch to the top-centre 'Bar' layout, and TOUCH_MIN_SCALE = 1.2 keeps tiles near 48 px. POINTER_MIN_SCALE = 0.8 still shrinks the UI below its authored size on small laptops.
The layout derive checks Responsive.inputKind() == 'Touch' or sizeClass() == 'Compact', and inputKind is read from UserInputService.PreferredInput.
The Bar is anchored top-centre with a 20 px margin inside a ScreenGui using ScreenInsets.CoreUISafeInsets, away from the bottom-left and bottom-right controls.
The title keeps TextScaled with UITextSizeConstraint MaxTextSize = TITLE_MAX_TEXT_SIZE (24), not multiplied by the scale, so the title stays capped at 24 real px on 4K.
Valid Vide bindings and derives at component scope, all checks pass, and selection still works. Hotkey labels and the BlockPlacer.HotkeyLabels export add some scope.

UI/Screen.luau keeps realViewport, realInset, prefersTouch and isLargeDisplay as sources, refreshed on ViewportSize, CurrentCamera, TopbarInset, ViewportDisplaySize and PreferredInput changes, with reactive getters on top.

criteria.criterion: 2. Large screens grow via one UIScale
criteria.note: screenGui.luau adds one UIScale bound to Screen.uiScale (short side / 1080, clamped 1 to 3, with a TV boost).

criteria.criterion: 3. Small screens change layout, not shrink
criteria.note: MINIMUM_SCALE = 1 means the UI never shrinks. Phones get the 'Row' layout with 56 px swatches in 68 px wide tiles.
isTouchLayout() returns prefersTouch() or isPhone(), where prefersTouch comes from PreferredInput == Touch.
The Row is anchored top-right at UDim2.new(1,-12,0,12) inside CoreUISafeInsets, sized so it starts right of the thumbstick region on a 667 px wide phone.
The title drops TextScaled and the UITextSizeConstraint for a fixed TextSize = 24, which the root UIScale grows.

Valid Vide (metrics derive, all props bound) and all checks pass. Rewriting everything to const and @game string requires is churn and a possible runtime risk, and the story and README files are extras.

strengths: Clean Responsive module of live sources with size classes and canvas size in design units
The Root frame sized 1/scale under the UIScale keeps scale-based positions meaningful
Bar layout at top centre with a 1.2 minimum touch scale gives finger-sized tiles
weaknesses: Title UITextSizeConstraint is not scaled, so the title doesn't grow on 4K
Pointer minimum scale of 0.8 shrinks the UI below its authored size on small screens

strengths: Fixed TextSize lets the title grow with the UIScale
Scale never drops below 1, and phones get a dedicated Row layout with large tiles
Screen module tracks the topbar inset and display size, with a documented reusable screenGui wrapper
weaknesses: Gratuitous const and string-require rewrite of existing files
Screen.uiScale is recomputed on every read rather than derived (minor)
Title hidden in the Row layout, so the selected name appears only as bold tile text
